ownership_reason: Only the gold walks a source in order and decides what is returned when the walk runs out; it is handed the Enumeration itself, so it alone can return the nth element and, when there are fewer elements, the very Enumeration it was given, which the facade documents ('returning an empty Iterator (resp. Enumeration) if the nth value does not exist') and testIndex asserts (test.equals(en) && !en.hasMoreElements()). Hops 1-4 can only change what they hand on: an iterator view of the Enumeration makes the exhausted case return the view, a List copy makes it throw at the List read, and nothing can be recovered after the gold has returned. The convention is pinned outside the gold: CollectionUtils.get walks an Enumeration to its index-th element like an Iterator (testGet), CollectionUtils.size and sizeIsEmpty treat an Enumeration like an Iterator (testSize_Enumeration, testSizeIsEmpty_Enumeration), IteratorUtils.getIterator reads an Enumeration through an EnumerationIterator, and the facade's and index(Object,int)'s javadoc list the enumeration case.
